title: Small Tools
subtitle: Small repositories I authored or contributed to for engineering, research, job-search materials, and agent collaboration. They come from recurring workflow problems: context drift, scattered research, repeated resume maintenance, and the need to bring agents into tasks reliably.
viewAllDescription: Browse the small tools behind my context management, research, and agent collaboration workflows.

project-context-meta-skill.title: Project Context Meta-Skill
project-context-meta-skill.summary: A context-governance tool for long-running AI-assisted engineering work. It is not just about giving the agent more memory; it separates user intent, stable specifications, historical decisions, and current focus so a task remains traceable across conversations and phases.
points: Separates RAW_REQUIREMENTS, SPEC, ROADMAP, and ACTIVE_TASK into different responsibilities: request capture, stable system behavior, decision history, and current execution focus.
Packages task startup, spec sync, task archiving, and commit assistance as reusable skills that can move between projects.
Builds challenge, trade-off analysis, and scope checks into the workflow so vague goals and over-engineering surface early.
The practical value is less repeated context explanation and fewer regressions caused by long-session context drift.

research-skills.title: Engineering Research Skills
research-skills.summary: A research workflow for engineering, product, market, and scientific judgment. It targets situations where the question is broad, the information is noisy, and the final output still needs to support a decision.
points: Turns ad hoc searching into a reusable process across Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, and similar AI tools.
Uses AnySearch as the default real-time retrieval entry point for technical selection, product opportunity analysis, competitor research, and paper or open-source evaluation.
Requires outputs to include not only collected facts, but also evidence, boundaries, risks, and actionable recommendations.
The value is turning uncertain information into material that can be discussed, challenged, and used for the next engineering step.

latex-resume.title: LaTeX Resume Builder
latex-resume.summary: A private in-progress resume project exploring how to generate multilingual, role-targeted resumes with LaTeX. It addresses a real maintenance problem: the same experience needs different language variants, role emphasis, and length constraints without drifting out of sync.
points: Explores structured content for Chinese, English, and other variants by separating experience content, project descriptions, skill phrasing, and layout control.
Targets fast adaptation for different roles by changing the emphasis across projects, skills, and experience without manually rebuilding each file.
Uses LaTeX for stable formatting and version control, making the resume closer to a long-lived content asset than a one-off document.
May eventually become a skill, template system, or another automation tool for a reusable job-search material workflow.

anysearch-skill.title: AnySearch Skill Contribution
anysearch-skill.summary: A contribution to the upstream AnySearch Skill, bringing real-time retrieval into AI agent workflows. The core need is clear: when agents research, debug, or evaluate, they need a stable way to access current web results and page content instead of relying on static model memory.
points: The contribution was merged upstream, showing the full open-source path from forked implementation to accepted community change.
Supports multiple runtimes including Python, Node.js, PowerShell, and Shell to reduce integration friction across systems and agent environments.
Covers general search, vertical search, parallel batch search, and page extraction so research can move from asking the model to checking evidence.
The value is turning web retrieval into a stable tool interface instead of a one-off command or manual copy-paste step.

crater-prompt.title: Crater Agent Prompts
crater-prompt.summary: An archived prompt repository created before the skill mechanism existed, used to guide AI agents in Crater development. It came from a concrete need: helping an AI assistant understand a complex project's context, norms, and constraints without restarting from scratch each time.
points: Turns Crater project experience, recurring requirements, and collaboration habits into prompts that an agent can consume directly.
Helps agents enter the existing engineering context faster, reducing invalid implementations caused by missing project constraints.
Although document-oriented, it served as an early tool by externalizing implicit experience into a reusable collaboration entry point.
Preserves the evolution from prompt assets toward structured agent skills.
